import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib as mpl
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import from_levels_and_colors

my_cmap = mpl.cm.viridis
bounds = np.arange(10)
nb_colors = len(bounds) + 1
colors = my_cmap(np.linspace(100, 255, nb_colors).astype(int))
my_cmap, my_norm = from_levels_and_colors(bounds, colors, extend='both')

plt.figure(figsize=(5, 1))
ax = plt.subplot(111)
cbar = mpl.colorbar.ColorbarBase(ax, cmap=my_cmap, norm=my_norm,
                                 orientation='horizontal', drawedges=True)
fig = plt.gcf()
fig.canvas.draw()
segs = cbar.dividers.get_segments()
print('n_segments:', len(segs))
print('first:', np.round(segs[0], 3).tolist())
print('last :', np.round(segs[-1], 3).tolist())
# extremity edges must be at y=0 and y=1 spanning x 0..1
ok_first = np.allclose(segs[0][:, 1], 0) and np.allclose(segs[0][:, 0], [0, 1])
ok_last = np.allclose(segs[-1][:, 1], 1) and np.allclose(segs[-1][:, 0], [0, 1])
print('lower extremity edge drawn:', ok_first)
print('upper extremity edge drawn:', ok_last)
# also check 'neither' case still trims both ends
cbar2 = mpl.colorbar.ColorbarBase(plt.subplot(122), cmap=my_cmap, norm=my_norm,
                                  orientation='horizontal', drawedges=True,
                                  extend='neither')
fig.canvas.draw()
segs2 = cbar2.dividers.get_segments()
print('neither: n_segments:', len(segs2), '(expect nb_colors-1 =', nb_colors-1, ')')
fig.savefig('C:/Windows/Temp/cbar_fix.png', dpi=100)
print('saved C:/Windows/Temp/cbar_fix.png')
EOF
